title: Psychometric assessment of the Basic Empathy Scale (BES-20) in Ecuadorian adolescents: A bifactor modeling approach and measurement invariance across sex.
abstract: The present study examined the psychometric properties, structural validity, wording-related method effects, and sex measurement invariance of the Basic Empathy Scale (BES-20) among Ecuadorian adolescents, addressing the need for culturally adapted measures of empathy in Latin American contexts. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional, and instrumental design, valid data were collected from 635 adolescents (M= 15.05, SD = 2.32). For multi-group measurement invariance analyses across self-reported sex, a balanced subsample of 626 participants (313 male and 313 female participants) was analyzed after excluding nine participants who identified outside the two binary categories. To account for the ordinal nature of the five-point Likert response scale, analyses were conducted using Diagonally Weighted Least Squares (DWLS/WLSMV) estimation on polychoric correlation matrices. Confirmatory factor analyses indicated that preliminary solutions grouping reverse-worded items into a third factor (often labeled "Emotional Insensitivity") were consistent with a wording-related method artifact rather than a substantive psychological dimension. Incorporating an orthogonal method factor for the seven reverse-worded items within a bifactor-type confirmatory model recovered the original two-factor structure (Cognitive and Affective Empathy) with good model fit (CFI = 0.963, TLI = 0.957, SRMR = 0.060, RMSEA = 0.068, 90% CI [0.062, 0.073]), outperforming the correlated two-factor (CFI = 0.721) and unconstrained three-factor (CFI = 0.885) models. Direct substantive items exhibited statistically significant factor loadings (λ = 0.451-0.795), and subscale reliability estimated via McDonald's omega (ω) was adequate for direct indicators of Cognitive Empathy (k = 6, ω = 0.775) and Affective Empathy (k = 7, ω = 0.799). Furthermore, sequential multi-group CFA supported full scalar measurement invariance across self-reported sex (∣ΔCFI∣ ≤ 0.007 < 0.010; ∣ΔRMSEA∣ ≤ 0.005 < 0.015), indicating that latent empathy scores are comparable across male and female adolescents in this sample. Overall, findings suggest that negatively phrased items introduce systematic method variance in adolescent self-reports. Practically, the adapted BES-20 provides a structurally sound tool for educational and prevention research in Ecuador, with potential applicability in clinical settings pending validation with clinical samples.
